bull.b: Product-led growth is more repeatable than a license-driven spike because it reflects customer shipments and deployment activity. Sustained adoption across IoT programs could improve revenue visibility as production volumes scale.

Conversion of design wins into mass production provides tangible evidence of commercial adoption and creates a multi-year base of potential product revenue. A backlog extending into 2027 may improve demand visibility and operating leverage.

Debt repayment reduces refinancing risk, interest obligations, and financial complexity while preserving greater flexibility to fund product development. The stronger capital structure supports execution of the IoT and RF growth roadmap.

bear.b: Large recurring losses indicate that current revenue scale is insufficient to support the cost base. Unless product growth and cost reductions materially improve operating leverage, profitability remains uncertain and shareholder dilution risk may persist.

Ongoing cash consumption limits the company’s ability to self-fund research, inventory, and commercialization. Even with improved liquidity, continued losses could require asset sales, financing, or other measures before breakeven.

Lower product margins and persistent supply constraints can restrict gross-profit recovery even as shipments grow. Reliance on multisourcing, customer price increases, and future licensing deals makes the path to breakeven execution-sensitive.
